title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching, quant profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Jordan Patel
description:
Background: customers running high-throughput evals and production traffic have asked for safer, opinionated defaults for batching/caching and first-class quantization profiles so we can reduce per-token cost without regressing latency or quality. This PR implements a coordinated set of changes: 1) autotune defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching (runtime-level heuristics + per-model defaults), 2) a small declarative quantization profile format and runtime hooks to prefer lower-precision kernels where quality budgets allow, and 3) unit-economics tooling (uecon) that computes per-route token cost estimates and suggests the autotune profile that meets a target cost/latency tradeoff. The description below is a single continuous string that contains the motivation, changes, testing notes, and rollout plan.

Changes:
- runtime/autotune: new default heuristics that pick batch sizes based on p95 latency and tail distribution, with conservative backoff for cold-cache workloads so we don't regress cold-start latency.
- runtime/cache: KV prefix caching defaults (TTL and memory budget) exposed as config with sane defaults and ability to opt-out per-route.
- model-registry: added quant_profiles/ schema + three example profiles (fp16, int8-asymmetric, int8-gptq) and profile selection policy.
- redwood-optimize/uecon: new CLI and backend job that ingests recent usage traces (token counts, model variant, latency) and computes per-route unit economics and suggested profile.
- console: new UI panels for UEcon summary and suggested profile rollout.

Checklist:
- [x] Runtime heuristics implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Quant profiles schema and selection API + integration tests
- [x] UEcon computation job and CLI + e2e tests against synthetic traces
- [x] Dashboard panels + feature flag behind `uecon-ui`
- [x] Documentation and migration notes added
- [x] Perf canary results verified on staging

Motivation and constraints: We want a low-risk default that benefits many customers while making it easy to opt into more aggressive profiles. The autotune heuristics are intentionally conservative: default batch size targets p50 throughput improvements but enforce p95 latency SLOs from the route. Quant profiles are only applied when model validation (on a small eval set) passes the configured quality threshold. UEcon tooling runs periodically and emits recommendations; applying recommendations requires an explicit rollout (canary then full rollout) via the existing rollout APIs.

Migration notes:
- New default behavior is behind a feature flag `autotune-defaults-v2` for 2 weeks, enabled for internal and beta tenants initially.
- Operators can override per-route via route config: {autotune: {enabled: false}} or set quant_profile: "none".
- Existing routes without explicit settings will inherit the new conservative defaults.

Testing and results:
- Unit and integration tests added under packages/runtime and redwood-optimize.
- Staging perf-canary showed median token cost reduction of ~9-12% across three representative workloads; p95 latency remained within 3% of baseline (SLOs preserved).
- Quantized model variants (int8-gptq) showed estimated 20-35% cost reduction on GPU-backed hosts for batch-friendly workloads; quality checks on held-out prompts passed thresholds for the provided example profiles.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag enable for internal tenants and run uecon job for 48h to gather recommended profiles.
2) Canary apply recommended profiles to <5% of traffic for target routes, monitor p95 latency & quality signals.
3) If stable, increase rollout to 100% with opt-out notice.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the autotune selection logic (packages/runtime/autotune/defaults.py) and the decision surface for applying quant profiles (model-registry/quant_profiles.md + selection hooks). The UEcon job is intentionally conservative in suggestions: it only recommends a profile if projected savings exceed a configurable threshold and quality checks pass.

review_comments: Ava Chen: Left a few comments on the autotune backoff logic. Can we ensure cold-start paths explicitly cap batch growth for first 10s after a VM spin-up?
Jordan Patel: Good catch - added an explicit cold_start window parameter with tests. See packages/runtime/src/autotune/defaults.py line ~120.
Diego Martinez: The quant profile selection looks fine, but please add a short-circuit when model size < 7B to avoid applying int8-gptq heuristics that are tuned for larger models.
Jordan Patel: Added short-circuit and unit test; updated quant_profiles.yaml with min_model_size field.
Priya Nair: UEcon output looks promising. One request: expose per-token GPU cost and per-token CPU cost separately in the CLI output so SRE teams can attribute savings to infra types.
Jordan Patel: Exposed separate cost buckets in uecon CLI output (redwood-optimize/uecon/cli.py).
release_notes:
- Added conservative autotune defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching to reduce per-token costs while preserving latency SLOs.
- Introduced declarative quantization profiles with three example profiles (fp16, int8-asymmetric, int8-gptq).
- Added UEcon tooling (CLI + job) to compute per-route unit economics and produce suggested profiles.
- Console panels for UEcon are available behind the `uecon-ui` feature flag.
notes: This PR touches runtime and model-registry surfaces; operators should monitor the uecon suggestions and perform canaries before broad rollout. The feature flags ensure we can quickly revert defaults if needed.
